metadata.title: Madelung Rule Exceptions — Viz Riff
metadata.purpose: Riff critique of the Madelung exceptions D3 simulation — bar chart threshold encoding, and the three-way contradiction when K falls below the exception threshold.

beats.narration_text: Hola. Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked Claude to build a visualization of why chromium and copper break the Madelung filling rule. This is what came back. We are judging the visualization, not the quantum mechanics.

props.command: write me a visualization for Madelung rule exceptions in 3d transition metals
props.runningText: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for Madelung rule exceptions in 3d transition metals.
output: ✓ D3 CDN — element selector + K slider
✓ exchange gain vs promotion cost bar chart

beats.narration_text: Ten element buttons — scandium through zinc. Chromium and copper carry red borders and a dot. One slider: K, the exchange integral, zero to forty hundredths of an electron-volt. Two panels: energy bars on the left, orbital diagram on the right. A physics console below.

K is the exchange energy bonus for each pair of parallel-spin electrons. For chromium, promoting one four-s electron to three-d gains four parallel pairs. The left panel shows this gain against the fixed promotion cost, on the same scale. When the gain bar clears the cost bar, the verdict flips. That threshold is what the slider is designed to sweep.

What the visualization gets right: the bar chart encodes the actual physics argument. Exchange gain and promotion cost are the same unit on the same axis — a student sees exactly when one overtakes the other, not just that it does. The threshold is drawn, not explained. The orbital diagram is equally direct: five boxes for five d-orbitals, spin arrows inside, Madelung versus actual configuration side by side. The difference is traceable by eye before the label names it.

Two encoding failures. Drop K to zero-point-zero-two: the verdict correctly flips green — Madelung rule holds. But chromium's button still carries a red exception border. The orbital diagram still reads actual equals exception. And the physics console — which labels itself hardcoded K equals zero-point-eighteen — reports exception predicted for a different K than the one on screen. Three signals, three different answers. The exception borders and config labels are set once at page load from hardcoded data and never re-evaluated. A student dragging K to zero hears no exception from the verdict and permanent exception from everything else.

Let's recap with Claude. The bar chart threshold crossing is the right encoding. Element borders are hardcoded — they never respond to K. The physics console is frozen at K equals zero-point-eighteen. Use this after the Madelung lecture, and fix the console first.

artifactLines: Bar chart threshold crossing — correct encoding
Element borders hardcoded — never respond to K slider
Physics console frozen at K=0.18 regardless of state
Use after Madelung lecture; fix the console first

beats.narration_text: I have a Madelung rule exceptions simulation where a K slider controls the exchange integral. The exception borders on element buttons are hardcoded at page load and don't respond to K. Fix three things: one — make exception markers on each element button update whenever K changes; two — update the physics console's P1 and P2 checks to use the current K value, not a hardcoded zero-point-eighteen; three — add a threshold marker on the energy bars showing exactly where the exception boundary falls for the selected element.
